newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Lloyds Chemists awaits final offers.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Lloyds Chemists awaits final offers.

text.p: Britain's Lloyds Chemists Plc told its shareholders on Tuesday they would be wise to let the two rival takeover bidders for the company table their final offers before opting to take up either of them.
Suitors Unichem Plc and Germany's Gehe AG -- Europe's largest drug distributor -- have been locked in a takeover battle for the pharmacy chain since February.
Lloyds' board said in a statement to shareholders in response to bids from both firms, that it realised they offered more value than Lloyds could achieve alone in the short term.
Recognising that neither bidder had declared its offer final, however, it said it continued "to advise shareholders to take no action in relation to their shareholdings" for now.

Lloyds said its board felt "that the offers from UniChem and Gehe each provide shareholders with more value than the board believes could be achieved...as an independent company in the immediate future".

It also said an acquisition would represent "a major strategic opportunity" for both UniChem and Gehe -- recognising that both the pharmaceutical wholesalers and retailers could enhance revenues and cut costs through a deal.

The latest round of bids, following an interruption in the spring when both companies' first bids were referred to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission, pits a cash and shares offer from UniChem against a proposed all-cash deal from Gehe.
UniChem's bid, tabled on October 18, offers 16 new Unichem shares and 926p in cash for every 10 Lloyds shares.
It initially valued Lloyds at 657.6 million pounds ($1.1 billion), though Unichem's share price has since slipped and industry sources said it was now worth closer to 635 million.
Gehe's response, announced on November 5 but not yet formally posted to shareholders, was an all-cash offer of 500p per ordinary share valuing Lloyds at 650.6 million pounds.
UniChem, which already owns 9.9 percent of Lloyds, has said it believes Gehe could obtain less value from Lloyds Chemists in on-going cost savings and revenue benefits than it would.
Gehe has emphasised on the other hand that its offer is inherently less risky as it is only in cash.
Both companies have been told, after the MMC inquiry, that they would have to make some disposals if they were to succesfully complete an acquisition of Lloyds.
Since Unichem launched its latest bid, Lloyds shares have traded sideways at around 511 pence and were virtually unchanged at 512p, up 1/2p, by 1430 GMT on Tuesday.
